metadata.source_status: Real engineering work: fifth report in the Layer 1 hardening series. Reverse-engineered a working Google News link decoder (the old url= regex never matched modern redirect links), caught a classification-ordering near-miss before deploying, and verified across 3 escalating rounds (20/20, 16/16, 6/6 end-to-end). Two limitations honestly flagged: unverified against the fellow's live n8n instance, and ~400 extra requests/run. Every claim traces to B3-VERIFICATION.md (2026-08-31). See SOURCES.md and FACTCHECK.md.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sai Pranavi J. This video is about a link that looked like a real article URL but wasn't — every Google News item in this pipeline was storing a dead-end redirect — and the fix that had to reverse-engineer how Google News resolves its own links.
beats.new_visual_element: Personal-intro card: fellow's name + one-line summary of what the video covers, spoken

shot.note: Same pattern as this fellow's other episodes' B01.

beats.narration_text: Every item this pipeline pulls from Google News stores a link. Click it, and it doesn't take you to the article. It takes you back to Google. The link was never real to begin with.
beats.new_visual_element: A feed item card, a link, a click animation landing back on a Google News icon instead of an article

shot.note: Generic feed-item visual, no real product named.

beats.narration_text: The code that was supposed to fix this looked for a url equals parameter in the link and pulled the real address out of it. That trick used to work. It doesn't anymore, modern Google News links don't carry that parameter at all. The regex had nothing to match, so it silently did nothing, every single time.
beats.new_visual_element: The regex url=([^&]+) next to a real link (news.google.com/rss/articles/<opaque-id>?oc=5) with the missing parameter highlighted as absent

shot.note: [Source: B3-VERIFICATION.md 'The bug'] Regex and real link shown verbatim, not paraphrased.

beats.narration_text: Following the redirect doesn't help either, it just bounces back to the same address. The only way to get the real URL is the way the Google News page itself gets it: the page embeds a signed id, timestamp, and signature, and posts them to an internal Google endpoint, which hands back the real article link.
beats.new_visual_element: Flow diagram: redirect page -> extract id/timestamp/signature -> POST to internal endpoint -> real URL returned, with a caveat label 'reverse-engineered — not a documented/official API'

shot.note: [Source: B3-VERIFICATION.md 'Why it's not a simple regex/302 fix' and 'The fix'] On-screen caveat label required per FACTCHECK.md item #1 (resolved) — must be clearly legible, not a tiny afterthought.

beats.narration_text: Here's the catch that almost shipped. The step that labels each item by regulator checks the link's domain, news.google.com means Google News. The old code checked that before trying to unwrap the link, which never mattered, because unwrapping never actually worked. The moment unwrapping started working, checking the domain afterward would have broken that labeling for every single item, quietly undoing two weeks of fixes. Caught before it ever shipped, by classifying on the original link first.
beats.new_visual_element: Two call-order diagrams side by side: old (classify AFTER unwrap, now broken) vs. fixed (classify BEFORE unwrap, using the unwrapped link only for display)

shot.note: [Source: B3-VERIFICATION.md 'Critical ordering fix, caught before deploying'] Both call orders shown together, not sequential-only.

beats.narration_text: I tested this three times, each closer to the real system. First a script: twenty out of twenty links resolved. Then the exact code, ported: sixteen out of sixteen. Then the actual updated node, run the way the real pipeline runs it: six real Google News items, all six resolved to real working articles, and all six still correctly labeled, proving the ordering fix works too.
beats.new_visual_element: Three-round results, escalating: 20/20 -> 16/16 -> 6/6, with the final round's real resolved URLs shown

shot.note: [Source: B3-VERIFICATION.md 'Live verification'] All 3 rounds visible, not just the strongest.

beats.narration_text: Two things I'm not claiming. I haven't verified this exact code runs the same way on the fellow's actual n8n instance, only on the workflow file. And this adds real cost: about four hundred extra requests per run, spread out on purpose so it doesn't look like a burst. If Google changes how this works, the pipeline won't go quiet about it, it logs exactly how many links resolved and how many fell back.
beats.new_visual_element: Two limitation cards: 'not yet verified on live n8n' and 'adds ~400 requests/run, by design not parallelized', plus the visibility log line (Google News links seen: N, unwrapped: M, fell back: N-M)

shot.note: [Source: B3-VERIFICATION.md 'Visibility, not silent degradation' and 'What's NOT verified'] Kept at full weight per FACTCHECK.md resolution — do not soften.

beats.narration_text: A fix that works today isn't finished until you've asked what happens the day it stops working, and made sure you'll actually notice.
